facts.raw_span: A 47-year-old man
no significant medical history
his father was diagnosed with COVID-19
general malaise without fever or respiratory symptoms
ST-segment elevation on electrocardiogram
Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during transport to hospital
No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
Thrombopenia
SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Dorsal pulmonary infiltrative shadow and bilateral pleural effusions
diffuse contraction band necrosis with several lymphocytes in cardiac muscle

support_spans: ST-segment elevation on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab

concepts.why: The presence of ST-segment elevation, elevated cardiac markers, and diffuse contraction band necrosis in the context of a positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test suggests myocarditis due to COVID-19.

support_spans: ST-segment elevation on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
contradict_spans: No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
concepts.why: The presence of ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac markers could suggest acute coronary syndrome, but the absence of coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis makes this less likely.

support_spans: Thrombopenia
concepts.why: The presence of thrombopenia could suggest thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, but this diagnosis would require additional findings such as microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and renal failure.

support_spans: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Dorsal pulmonary infiltrative shadow and bilateral pleural effusions
contradict_spans: general malaise without fever or respiratory symptoms
concepts.why: The presence of a positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test and pulmonary infiltrative shadow suggests severe COVID-19 pneumonia, but the initial absence of respiratory symptoms makes this less likely.

support_spans: Thrombopenia
concepts.why: The presence of thrombopenia could suggest disseminated intravascular coagulation, but this diagnosis would require additional findings such as prolonged prothrombin time and decreased fibrinogen level.
It explains the cardiopulmonary arrest and the absence of coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis, suggesting a non-atherosclerotic cause of myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of diffuse contraction band necrosis with several lymphocytes in cardiac muscle and the positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test decided it.
